 Bryan Cranston, a two-time Tony Award winner, will return to Broadway next spring to star in a revival of “ All My Sons ,” Arthur Miller’s disquieting play about a family torn apart by its association with the manufacturing of defective airplane parts that resulted in the deaths of World War II pilots.
 The production, which will also star Marianne Jean-Baptiste , was announced Monday, and joins a parade of starry plays dominating the boards on Broadway this season.
 Here’s what we know so far.
 When is this happening?
 “All My Sons” is scheduled to start previews March 30, with an opening on April 13 for a 13-week run at the August Wilson Theater, where “ Paranormal Activity ” has been running since August.
 Tell me about this play.
 “All My Sons” was first staged on Broadway in 1947 , and was inspired by a scandal over the approval of defective parts for use in military aircraft. The play concerns a family whose patriarch runs a factory that makes aircraft parts; the family is wracked not only by his role in the failure of those parts — his business partner took the blame, but the question of who is responsible is a subject of the play — and also by the disappearance of a son in military action.
 Miller’s first big success (he won a Tony Award for best author), it contains themes about the toxicity of greed and the corrupting potential of the American dream. It has been revived on Broadway three times since, in 1987 , 2008 and 2019 .
 Who is involved in the production?
 The director is Ivo van Hove, a Belgian theater maker known for his experimental work. Van Hove won a Tony Award in 2016 for directing a revival of another Miller classic, “ A View From the Bridge .” His production of “All My Sons” debuted last fall in London, where it also starred Cranston and Jean-Baptiste. It went on to win the 2026 Olivier Award for best revival.
 “There is something in Miller’s material that suits van Hove’s foreboding aesthetic,” the critic Houman Barekat wrote in reviewing the London production for The New York Times, adding, “The sense of destiny making its inexorable claim; the doomed protagonist gradually losing his grip on events.”
 Cranston, who starred in the acclaimed TV series “ Breaking Bad ,” has appeared on Broadway twice, and won Tony Awards both times: in 2014 for “ All the Way ” and in 2019 for “ Network ,” which was also directed by van Hove.
 Cranston will play the factory owner, Joe Keller; Jean-Baptiste, an Oscar nominee for “ Secrets & Lies ,” will play his character’s wife, Kate. Other members of the cast have not yet been announced.
 The show’s lead producers are Wessex Grove and Gavin Kalin .
 Michael Paulson is the theater reporter for The Times.
